verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission is set for April 2025.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: R1: 'in 2026 NASA is talking'; R2: launch at '6:35 p.m. EDT' in 2026 context; R3: 'March 31, 2026'; R6: 'April 1, 2026'; R7: 'April 1'
verifications.reasoning: All references specify 2026, not 2025, directly contradicting the claim's date.

verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'The approximately 10-day Artemis II mission'; R3: '10-day journey'; R4: '10-day mission'; R6: 'The 10-day Artemis II mission'; R7: 'about 10 days'; R8: '10-day mission'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly state it is a 10-day mission.

verifications.claim: Artemis II will fly four astronauts around the Moon and back to Earth.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, and Christina Koch, along with CSA astronaut Jeremy Hansen... around the Moon and back'; R3: 'send four astronauts on a 10-day journey from Earth around the moon'; R4: 'flying four astronauts on a 10-day mission around the moon'; R6: 'four astronauts... around the Moon'
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly name four astronauts and describe the lunar flyby trajectory back to Earth.

verifications.claim: Artemis II is the first crewed flight test of the Space Launch System (SLS) rocket and Orion spacecraft.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'the first crewed flight under NASA’s Artemis campaign... SLS rocket, with the Orion spacecraft'; R6: 'first crewed mission — of NASA’s Artemis program... SLS rocket, and the Orion spacecraft'; R7: 'first crewed flight of NASA’s Artemis program'
verifications.reasoning: Directly described as the first crewed test of SLS and Orion after uncrewed Artemis I.

verifications.claim: Artemis II validates life-support systems with astronauts for deep space travel.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'test the systems and hardware needed... life‑support systems'; R6: 'flight test Orion’s life-support systems with astronauts on board... deep space'; R7: 'validate the life-support and environmental control systems... in deep space'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm validation/testing of life-support systems with crew in deep space.

verifications.claim: Artemis II will test the Orion spacecraft's environmental control and life-support systems (power, propulsion, and crew safety) with a human crew for the first time.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'test life-support systems and critical operations in deep space... SAWs... power... propulsion'; R6: 'flight test Orion’s life-support systems with astronauts... power... propulsion'; R7: 'life-support and environmental control systems... with humans aboard'
verifications.reasoning: Directly supports testing ECLSS including power, propulsion, crew safety with humans first time; specifics match closely.

verifications.claim: Artemis II will fly astronauts further into space than ever before.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'send the crew farther from Earth than any previous human mission... breaking the record'; R6: 'break Apollo 13’s record... farthest distance humans have traveled'; R7: 'farther from Earth than any humans have traveled before'; R8: 'broken a distance record... farther from Earth than any previous crewed mission'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources state it will exceed previous records like Apollo 13.

verifications.claim: Artemis II will venture into deep Earth orbit and around the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'high‑space operations... outbound journey to the Moon'; R4: 'high elliptical orbit... around the moon'; R6: 'high elliptical orbit... around the Moon'; R7: 'initial orbit around Earth... toward the Moon'
verifications.reasoning: Describes path: Earth orbit (deep/high), then lunar flyby.

verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'Artemis I worked toward testing'; R6: 'follow-up mission to the uncrewed Artemis I mission in 2022'; R7: 'Artemis I, which launched in 2022... without a crew'

verifications.claim: Artemis II serves as a bridge between the uncrewed Artemis I and future lunar surface missions.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R6: 'follow-up mission to the uncrewed Artemis I... paving the way for future lunar landings'; R7: 'builds on that success... before attempting a lunar landing on Artemis III'
verifications.reasoning: Directly positions it as intermediate step between Artemis I and landings.

verifications.claim: Artemis II will gather essential data on radiation shielding and human performance.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'gathering data to make it safer... radiation'; R5: 'radiation sensors... human health experiments... human physiology'; R8: 'studies of human physiology... radiation shelter construction demo'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm data collection on radiation and human performance/health.

verifications.claim: Artemis II will gather data on the safety of female astronauts.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R3: 'Women in particular are more prone to this damaging radiation... testing the shielding necessary to safely send female astronauts... Christina Koch... first woman to journey into deep space'
verifications.reasoning: Mentions radiation risks for women and Koch as first woman, implying data benefits females, but not specifically Artemis II gathering female-specific data (more Artemis I).

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew features astronauts from NASA and the Canadian Space Agency.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, and Christina Koch, along with CSA astronaut Jeremy Hansen'; R3: 'Canadian Space Agency, Jeremy Hansen'; R6: same crew names
verifications.reasoning: Explicitly lists NASA and CSA astronauts.

verifications.claim: Artemis II highlights international partnership with ESA, JAXA, and the UAE.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: R3: 'international contributions from... ESA, JAXA... UAE. Astronauts from these agencies will fly... on future Artemis missions.'
verifications.reasoning: Partnerships mentioned for Artemis program/future missions, not specifically Artemis II (which has CSA); Artemis II crew is NASA/CSA only.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew will perform detailed observations of the lunar surface.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: 'lunar observations operations... recording extensive observational data, taking photos'; R5: 'photograph and describe surface features'; R6: 'make observations and take photos of the far side of the Moon'
verifications.reasoning: Directly states crew will observe/photograph lunar surface.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew observations target geological features to guide future landing spots near the South Pole.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R4: 'tracking specific geological formations'; R5: 'study terrain... guide upcoming Artemis missions, including plans to land astronauts near the moon's south pole... which regions hold the greatest scientific promise'
verifications.reasoning: Observations of geological features to guide future landings including south pole, but not exclusively targeting south pole spots.

verifications.claim: Artemis II will prove that space technologies are safe for long-duration human spaceflight beyond low-Earth orbit.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R2: 'test the systems... paving the way for future lunar landings and Mars'; R6: 'test flight... essential as NASA intends to send astronauts on longer-duration missions'; R7: 'validate... systems that keep astronauts alive in deep space'
verifications.reasoning: Tests/validates systems for deep space, but 'prove safe for long-duration' is stronger than described (it's a test, not definitive proof).
